newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-YANKEES TAKE 3-2 SERIES LEAD ON PETTITTE FIVE-HITTER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-YANKEES TAKE 3-2 SERIES LEAD ON PETTITTE FIVE-HITTER.

text.p: Andy Pettitte and John Wetteland combined on a five-hitter and Cecil Fielder knocked in the only run of the game as the New York Yankees beat the Atlanta Braves 1-0 Thursday to head home with a three games to two lead in the World Series.
The run on a fourth-inning double by Fielder, who had three of the Yanks' four hits, was unearned, coming after a two-base error by Marquis Grissom in centre field on a ball hit by Charlie Hayes.

The 24-year-old Pettitte, this year's likely American League Cy Young winner, threw 8 1/3 innings with four strikeouts and three walks. He threw just 96 pitches, 59 of them strikes after a rough outing in Game 1 of the Series.
"The kid's got a lot of heart," said Yankee manager Joe Torre, whose team needs one more win to clinch the series.
"Tonight I had a good sinker going. I haven't had a sinker like that all year. It was unbelievable," said Pettitte.

Atlanta starter John Smoltz, the likely National League Cy Young winner, allowed just four hits with 10 strikeouts and three walks over eight innings in a pitching duel that came one day after a 14-run, 10-inning war of attrition won by New York.
"Smoltzie and he (Pettitte) went pitch for pitch," said Atlanta manager Bobby Cox. "There shouldn't have been a loser tonight."
"It's the best game I've ever pitched, given the circumstances," said Smoltz, who gave way to Mark Wohlers in the ninth after throwing 136 pitches. "I had nothing left when I left that mound."

John Wetteland got the save for two-thirds of an inning, getting two outs with a man on third. Paul O'Neill made a lunging catch on the run in deep right centre to retire pinch-hitter Luis Polonia for the last out.

The Yankees extended their record road win streak this post-season to 8-0 with the victory, which sent the best-of-seven Series back to New York for Game 6 and, if necessary, Game 7 on Saturday and Sunday.
The result was the reverse of Game 1 in New York, when Pettitte gave up seven runs in 2 1/3 innings and the Braves won 12-1. Smoltz yielded one run in six innings for that win.
"I'm thankful I could come out and give us a good outing after the horrible night the other night," said Pettitte. "My ball was running like crazy tonight."
The defending champion Braves threatened in the bottom of the ninth when Chipper Jones led off with a double and took third on Fred McGriff's ground-out.
Wetteland came on, and Javier Lopez slashed a grounder to Hayes at third base, who caught it sinking to his knees, held Jones at third and threw to first for the second out.
New York manager Joe Torre ordered an intentional walk to pinch-hitter Ryan Klesko and -- unlike a similar decision by Cox the night before -- it worked out.
Polonia fouled off six straight high fastballs and on the seventh smashed a liner to right that O'Neill just reached.
"I kept swinging at them and I kept fouling off," the ex-Yankee said. "Then the last one he came down a little bit and that's the one I got a good swing on."
Fielder's game-winner in the fourth with one out was the Yankees' second hit off Smoltz, and Fielder's second.
Hayes's long drive to right-centre ticked off Grissom's glove as right fielder Jermaine Dye crossed in front of him, but the usually smooth-fielding Grissom made no excuses.
"I made an error -- bottom line," said Grissom.
Fielder scored Hayes with a double into the left-field corner.
Torre played Fielder at first even though his regular first baseman, Tino Martinez, as a lefty would be the more orthodox choice against the right-handed Smoltz.
"I played him because he's probably had the most quality at-bats in this series," said Torre, who also praised the bulky Fielder's glovework at first base and his leadership.
"He's an athlete," said Torre. "He's got good hands. He knows what he's doing."
"The way I handle myself, I think that's probably my biggest plus with this ball club," said Fielder, the home run leader of the 1990s. "You have to stay professional."
In this Series, unusually, the home team has lost every game: "A game of inches," Cox observed. "The breaks haven't gone our way here in Atlanta."
Other than the ninth, the Braves' best chance came in the sixth, but Pettitte flashed some glove to stop them.
Smoltz led off with a single through the shortstop hole and Grissom, after failing to bunt, also singled.
Mark Lemke bunted but Pettitte snatched it up barehanded and daringly threw to third to nip the lead runner.
"I was going to third no matter what," said Pettitte.
Pettitte then got Chipper Jones to hit a comebacker and threw to second to start an inning-ending double play.
"Pettitte is a cat on the mound," said Cox.

In the fifth, Andruw Jones led off with a single but then Pettitte, who led the majors with 11 pick-offs during the regular season, threw to first as Jones took off for second, and the 19-year-old baserunner was caught stealing.
It was the last baseball game played in Fulton County Stadium. The Braves move to a new facility next door that was constructed for the Summer Olympics here.
